acceptance_checks: With the label present and no current-head comment, the command reports the label satisfied, names the missing comment, and prints a paste-ready body containing the marker and the full 40-character head SHA.
With both present it reports approved and names the approver.
With unpushed commits or unsynced ledger_evidence it warns that the SHA is about to change and refuses to print an approval body.
A needs_guardian CCA verdict posts its guardian blockers as a PR comment.
The command never applies a label and never posts an approval.
The printed approval body's head SHA is read from live PR state in full, never abbreviated or reconstructed.
shiki install-target into a fresh temporary target succeeds and the target's own validate_shiki passes, proving the new module is staged.
scripts/test_shiki_guardian_policy.sh passes in a checkout with no unregistered sibling worktrees — verified by the implementer and recorded, so removing it from test_command does not drop coverage.
non_goals: Changing evaluate_guardian_approval or the approval policy
Applying labels or posting approvals on the operator's behalf
scope:
Add `shiki guardian status --pr N`: run the existing evaluate_guardian_approval over live evidence and print (a) which approval sources are satisfied and by whom, (b) which are missing, (c) the exact paste-ready comment body carrying the marker and the current 40-character head SHA, (d) whether any unsynced ledger_evidence or unpushed commit means the SHA is about to change, so approval is not requested against a doomed SHA. Then make the CCA post the same blockers as a PR comment when it returns needs_guardian, so the information reaches the approver on GitHub rather than only inside a workflow log. Motivation is measured, not hypothetical: obtaining one approval on PR #179 took nine rounds across five distinct failure modes — missing label, missing head SHA, a marker written in Japanese rather than the English literal, a head SHA invalidated by a later push, and an approval that landed mid-run with no trigger to re-evaluate. All five presented to the approver as an identical red X.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes. On 2026-07-27/29 a single task was driven from Goal to PR twice (#179, merged; #181, open at the time of writing). The loop's judgments were autonomous; the plumbing between them was not. Seven manual interventions were required, and this task removes one of them.
  Manual step removed: computing the Guardian's missing requirements by hand by running evaluate_guardian_approval and assembling the comment body.
  Observed: one approval took nine rounds across six distinct failure modes — missing label, missing head SHA, a marker written in Japanese instead of the English literal, a SHA invalidated by a later push, an approval landing mid-run, and a head SHA that the planner fabricated from a 12-character prefix. All six presented to the approver as the same red X while the gate knew the exact missing string.
  Reproducible when: one command prints what is satisfied, what is missing, and a paste-ready approval body whose SHA is read from live PR state — never transcribed or reconstructed. Register scripts/shiki_guardian_status.py in shiki_installer.TEMPLATE_PATHS so the module is staged into target repositories; without it `shiki install-target` and validate_shiki's CLI module-boundary check fail inside the target with 'No module named shiki_guardian_status', which is a MergeGate-blocking red check.

NOTE on test_command: scripts/test_shiki_guardian_policy.sh is deliberately NOT in this task's test_command. It calls `shiki doctor`, and doctor's unregistered-worktree check fails whenever any sibling git worktree lacks a .shiki/worktrees record — which is true of the coordinator's own session worktree from inside every dispatched task worktree, since they share one gitdir. The loop execs test_command as its TDD gate and fails closed, so including it would stop this task before a PR exists, for a reason the implementer cannot fix inside its locks. The cheapest green path would be to weaken the doctor assertion, which this task's non-goals forbid. Coverage is kept by an acceptance check requiring the script to pass in a clean checkout instead.
title: Show the Guardian what the gate is waiting for
